correctness.rationale: A direct basis calculation yields ad_x on vertex idempotents as a weighted incidence map and on arrows as diagonal scalars. Shearing off the invertible arrow block proves the split Jordan decomposition; incidence kernel dimension equals κ(F) over any field. Counting weights and colors yields (1), a partition expansion yields (2), independent tree edge choices yield (3) and (4), and rank obstruction gives the iff characterization. Two source-file checkers exhaustively replay the original operator ranks for 11 finite test cases and a separate double-subset identity in four examples.

originality.rationale: Searches of published-finding corpus, the accessible history, and primary literature found results on Hochschild derivation structures and on full commutator fibers, but not the complete Jordan-canonical form and two-variable finite-field population of inner derivations for every loopless radical-square-zero quiver. A previously established commuting-probability invariant is exactly the scalar specialization of the new polynomial and is not reclaimed. The new proof combines a block shear, a weighted-incidence rank lemma, and an all-element color/support partition; an overlooked stronger theorem remains a priority risk.

value.rationale: The result computes an intrinsic all-element operator Jordan distribution and hence all centralizer dimensions in an infinite family of finite-dimensional algebras. The joint pair polynomial, not just an average commuting probability, is determined by a graphic-matroid state sum. The forest case gives an exact topology-independent binomial distribution and a maximal-rank square-zero inner-derivation iff test for forests. The invariant and its parameters are canonical and motivated by derivations/Hochschild theory; no arbitrary slice or rebranding of old cp results is claimed.
